name: Notre Dame Cathedral
overview: Notre-Dame de Paris is a masterpiece of French Gothic architecture and one of the most famous cathedrals in the world. Located on Île de la Cité, this medieval Catholic cathedral has been a symbol of Paris for over 850 years.
history: This Gothic masterpiece has witnessed 850 years of French history, from medieval times to modern tragedy. Built on the site of a Roman temple to Jupiter, then a Christian basilica, Notre-Dame became the spiritual heart of France. Here, Napoleon crowned himself Emperor in 1804 (snatching the crown from the Pope to show his power), Joan of Arc was posthumously declared innocent, and Te Deums were sung for military victories. During the French Revolution, anti-religious mobs destroyed statues, melted down bells for cannon metal, and turned the cathedral into a 'Temple of Reason' where they worshipped the goddess of Liberty! By the 1800s, it was nearly demolished until Victor Hugo's novel 'The Hunchback of Notre-Dame' sparked public outcry and led to its restoration by Viollet-le-Duc. The devastating 2019 fire that consumed its roof and spire shocked the world, but miraculously, the main structure and most treasures survived. Currently under restoration, it represents France's resilience - like the nation itself, Notre-Dame has survived wars, revolutions, and disasters, always rising again from the ashes.
highlights: Gothic architecture with flying buttresses and rose windows
Famous gargoyles overlooking Paris (pre-fire tower climb)
South Rose Window - one of the largest in the world
tips: Currently under restoration after 2019 fire - exterior viewing only. Visit nearby Sainte-Chapelle for spectacular stained glass. Point Zéro marker in front marks center of France. Best photographed from Square Jean XXIII behind cathedral.
